Rashi on Pesachim 98a:10:1.hebrew: לעולם דמית אחר חצות - ודקשיא לך: היאך יקרב שלמים, הא קבעתיה חצות ואידחי? ר' שמעון היא, דאמר בסדר יומא בפ' ב' שעירי (יומא סג:): בעלי חיים אין נדחין אלא מחמת מום או אתנן ומחיר שאינן ראויין; אבל למה שהוא ראוי יקרב, והאי חזי לשלמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:10:1.english: Actually, where he died after midday - And as for what was difficult for you: how can it be offered as a peace-offering, since midday established it [as a Paschal offering] and it was deferred? It is [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon, who said in Seder Yoma, in the chapter [entitled] Shenei Se'irei (Yoma 63b): Living animals are not deferred except on account of a blemish, or [being] a harlot's hire or a dog's price, which are unfit; rather, for whatever [offering] it is fit, it may be offered, and this [animal] is fit for a peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:11:1.hebrew: ה"ג רבינא אמר כגון שהפרישו אחר חצות ומתו בעליו אחר חצות - בנו נמנה עמו, יביאנו לשם פסח, דחיובא דפסח חיילא ברישא. אין בנו נמנה עמו, יביאנו לשלמים, דכיון דבחצות עדיין לא הופרש, אין כאן קבע לדחות. וקסבר תנא דידן חצות קבע, ולא כל שאר זמן שחיטה:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:11:1.english: This is the reading: Ravina said, [it is] a case where one separated it after midday and its owners died after midday - [If] his son is registered with him, he brings it for the sake of a Paschal offering, for the obligation of the Paschal offering took effect first. [If] his son is not registered with him, he brings it as a peace offering, for since at midday it had not yet been separated, there is no fixed designation here to reject [it]. And our Tanna holds [that] midday fixes [the status], and not all the rest of the time of slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:12:1.hebrew: הפסח שנתערב בזבחים - שלשה טלאים: א' של פסח, וא' של אשם, וא' של עולה, ונתערב הפסח ביניהן. כולם ירעו עד שיסתאבו, וימכרו, ויביא בדמי היפה שבהן עולה, דשמא היפה עולה היה, ובדמי היפה שבהן אשם, שמא היפה אשם היה, ובדמי היפה שבהן פסח — אם קודם הפסח [נסתאבו], ואם לאחר הפסח נסתאבו יביאנו שלמים — דשמא היפה פסח היה. ואותו מותר שהוא צריך להוסיף על השנים עד שיגיעו לדמי היפה שבהן, יפסיד מביתו — משלו. וא"ת: הרי הוא מחליף, שמביא שלמים בדמי האשם או בדמי העולה, והרי קדושת הבהמה חלתה על מעות דמיה, ואין משנין מקדושה לקדושה? כשבא לחללן להבהמות כך הוא עושה: אם יפה שבהן שוה סלע, מביא ג' סלעים מביתו, ונוטל הסלע האחת ואומר: כל מקום שהיא העולה, הרי מחוללת על הסלע זו, ויביא ממנו עולה; ונוטל סלע השנית ואומר: כל מקום שהוא האשם, הרי הוא מחולל על סלע זו, ומביא בו אשם; וכן לשלמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:12:1.english: A Paschal lamb that was intermingled with [other] offerings - [For example,] three lambs: one for a Paschal offering, and one for a guilt-offering, and one for a burnt-offering, and the Paschal lamb was intermingled among them. All of them shall graze until they become blemished, and they shall be sold, and he shall bring with the proceeds of the choicest of them a burnt-offering, for perhaps the choicest was the burnt-offering; and with the proceeds of the choicest of them a guilt-offering, [for] perhaps the choicest was the guilt-offering; and with the proceeds of the choicest of them a Paschal offering — if [they became blemished] before Passover, and if they became blemished after Passover, he shall bring it as a peace-offering — for perhaps the choicest was the Paschal offering. And that surplus that he needs to add to the [other] two until they reach the value of the choicest of them, he loses from his own house — from his own [pocket]. And if you say: Behold, he is exchanging [sanctities], for he brings a peace-offering with the proceeds of the guilt-offering or with the proceeds of the burnt-offering, and behold, the sanctity of the animal took effect upon the money of its proceeds, and we do not change from one sanctity to another sanctity? When he comes to redeem them onto the animals, this is what he does: if the choicest of them is worth a sela, he brings three sela'im from his house, and takes the first sela and says, "Wherever the burnt-offering is, behold it is redeemed onto this sela," and he brings from it a burnt-offering; and he takes the second sela and says, "Wherever the guilt-offering is, behold it is redeemed onto this sela," and he brings with it a guilt-offering; and similarly for the peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:13:1.hebrew: נתערב בבכורות - שמתן דמן ומתן דם הפסח שוה, ואין טעונין תנופת חזה ושוק ולא סמיכה ונסכים:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:13:1.english: It became intermingled with firstborn [animals] - For the application of their blood and the application of the blood of the Paschal lamb are the same, and they do not require waving of the breast and thigh, nor laying of hands, nor libations.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:13:2.hebrew: ר"ש אומר - אם כל החבורה כולה כהנים היו, יאכלו את כולם בו בלילה, ויקרב פסח לשם פסח כל מקום שהוא, והבכורות לשם בכור בכל מקום שהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:13:2.english: Rabbi Shimon says - If the entire company was all priests, they may eat all of them on that night, and the Paschal lamb shall be offered for the sake of a Paschal lamb wherever it is, and the firstborn [animals] for the sake of a firstborn [animal] wherever they are.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:1:1.english: One who separates his Paschal lamb and dies - Further on, [the Gemara] explains when he died.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:1:2.hebrew: לא יביאנו בנו אחריו לשם פסח - דהוה ליה פסח שמתו בעליו, ואין כאן מנויין:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:1:2.english: His son may not bring it after him for the purpose of a Paschal lamb - For it is a Paschal lamb whose owner died, and there are no registered [participants] here.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:2:1.hebrew: שמע מינה בעלי חיים נדחין - בהמה שנדחית בחיים דחויה דיחוי גמור, שאף לכשנראית למה שהיתה ראויה אינה קריבה, אלא רועה. דהא דתנן תרעה ולא קרבה שלמים, היא גופה, שזו היא ראייתה כמתחלה, שכל מותר פסח קרב שלמים. ודלא כר"ש, דאמר בעלי חיים אין נדחין בפרק שני שעירי (יומא דף סג:), דגמרינן מבעל מום שנדחה ולכשעבר מומו נראה. ומרישא נמי שמעינן לה, אלא משום דמהא שמעינן תלת נקט לה הכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:2:1.english: Conclude from it [that] living things are deferred - An animal that is deferred while alive is deferred with a complete deferral, such that even when it becomes fit for what it was [originally] fit for, it is not offered, but rather grazes. For this [ruling] that we learned in the Mishnah, "it shall graze" and is not offered as a peace-offering, is that very [case], for this is its fitness as at the beginning, since every remainder of a Paschal lamb is offered as a peace-offering. And [this is] not in accordance with R. Shimon, who says [that] living things are not deferred, in the chapter [entitled] Shenei Se'irei (Yoma 63b), for we derive [it] from a blemished [animal] that was deferred and when its blemish passed it became fit. And from the first clause [of the Mishnah] as well we learn it, except that because from this [clause] we learn three [laws], he stated it here.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:3:1.hebrew: ושמע מינה דחוי מעיקרא הוי דחוי - דהא נקבה או זכר בן שתי שנים, מתחלתו לא נראה למה שהוקדש, וקאמר ירעה ולא יקרב שלמים הוא עצמו. ואיכא למאן דאמר במסכת סוכה (דף לג:) דאין דחוי אלא הנראה ונדחה:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:3:1.english: And conclude from this [that] deferral at the outset is [considered] a deferral - For a female [animal] or a two-year-old male was not fit from its beginning for that for which it was consecrated, and [yet] it says [that] it shall pasture and it itself shall not be offered [as] a peace-offering. And there is one who says in Tractate Sukkah (33b) that there is no deferral except [for] what was fit and [then] became deferred.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:3:2.hebrew: ושמע מינה יש דחוי בדמים - כדפרישית בכמה מקומות, בגמ' מצינו לשון זה גבי הא דאמר רבי יוחנן: בהמה של שני שותפין, הקדיש חציה וחזר ולקח חציה, קדושה ואינה קריבה, שמע מינה תלת כו', כי הכא, ובמסכת קדושין (דף ז:) ובזבחים (דף יב.). ולמדתי פירושה ממסכת כריתות (דף כז.), דגרס התם בלשון הזה: ש"מ קדושת דמים נדחה. כלומר, שמע מינה אפילו דבר שלא קדש תחלה להקרבת גופו אלא לדמיו — כגון הקדיש חציה וחציה השני חולין — דחוי ליקרב לגופו בתחלת הקדישו, אינו קרב עוד לעולם, דהואיל ונדחה ידחה. ולא תימא אין דחוי בקדשים אלא הקדיש לגופו ונדחה מהקריב, אבל קדושת דמים לא אלימא למימר ביה תורת דחוי, ואי אתיא לה שעת הכשר הקרבה — כגון הכא דחזר ולקח חציה — תקרב. והכא נמי הכי פרישנא לה: יש דחוי בדמים, כגון נקיבה לפסח, לא חזיא גופה לפסח אלא כי אקדשה לדמים אקדשה, ואיידי דדחויה דלא חזיא לאקרובי גופה לדבר שהוקדשה לה, אמרינן תדחה לעולם, אפילו לאחר הפסח דכל מותר הפסח הוי שלמים ונקיבה לשלמים מחזא חזיא, דקתני מתני' דמי שלמים, אבל גופה לא; אלמא אלימא קדושת דמים לומר בה תורת דחוי. ולא אשכחן דפליגי תנאי בהא מילתא, מיהו טובא אשמעינן תשובת רבנו, ע"כ. ותמיהא לי: אמאי גרע ממותר הפסח שראוי לפסח, כדאמרינן בהאשה (לעיל פסחים דף פט:), ונטרחו ונייתי במותר:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:3:2.english: And conclude from this that there is deferral with regard to value - As I have explained in several places, in the Gemara we find this expression regarding that which Rabbi Yochanan said: "[Regarding] an animal belonging to two partners, [if one] consecrated half of it and then went back and bought [the other] half of it [and consecrated it], it is consecrated, yet it cannot be offered; conclude from it three things, etc." — like here, and in Tractate Kiddushin (7b) and in Zevachim (12a). And I learned its explanation from Tractate Keritot (27a), where it reads in this language: "Conclude from this that monetary sanctity is deferred." That is to say: conclude from this [that] even something that was not initially consecrated for the offering of its body, but only for its value — such as where he consecrated half of it while its other half remained unconsecrated — [since] it was deferred from being offered in its own body at the start of its consecration, it can never be offered again, for once it has been deferred, it remains deferred. And do not say [that] deferral applies to consecrated offerings only when he consecrated it for its own body and it was deferred from being offered, whereas monetary sanctity is not strong enough for the law of deferral to apply to it, so that if a time of fitness for offering arrives for it — such as here, where he went back and bought [the other] half — it may be offered. And here too we explain it thus: "There is deferral with regard to value" — for example, a female [consecrated] for a Paschal offering: its body is not fit for a Paschal offering, rather when he consecrated it, he consecrated it for its value; and since it is deferred in that its body is not fit to be offered for the purpose for which it was consecrated, we say it is deferred forever — even after Pesach, when any remainder of a Paschal offering becomes a peace-offering and a female is indeed fit for a peace-offering — for the Mishnah teaches [that it brings] the value of peace-offerings, but not its body itself; thus, monetary sanctity is strong enough for the law of deferral to apply to it. And we have not found that Tannaim disagree on this matter; however, our teacher's responsum taught us much [about this] — end [of the responsum]. And I wonder: why is [this case] worse than [that of] the remainder of a Paschal offering that is fit for a Paschal offering, as we say in [the chapter] HaIshah (above, Pesachim 89b): "Let them take the trouble and bring it as a remainder"?

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:4:1.hebrew: בנו נמנה עמו - אם היה בנו נמנה עמו, ועדיין יש לו בעלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:4:1.english: His son is registered with him - If his son was registered with him, and [thus] it still has owners.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:5:1.hebrew: אי נימא דמית קודם חצות - ובו ביום, הא חל אנינות עליה ברישא, ותו לא חיילא עליה חיובא דפסח להביאו בפני עצמן, כדתנן (לעיל פסחים דף צא.) וכולן אין שוחטין עליהן בפני עצמן. ומתני' קתני יביאנו, דמשמע הוא עצמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:5:1.english: If we say that he died before midday - and on that same day, behold, acute mourning took effect upon him first, and the obligation of the Paschal offering no longer takes effect upon him to bring it on his own, as we learned in a Mishnah (above, Pesachim 91a): "And [for] all of them, one may not slaughter [the Paschal offering] for them on their own." Yet the teaching [in the Tosefta] states, "he shall bring it," which implies he himself.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:6:1.hebrew: אלא דמת אחר חצות - דכיון דחיילא עליה דין פסח ברישא, שוחט לעצמו, ולא חיישינן שמא יביאוהו לבית הפסול, דמזהר זהיר משום חובת פסח דחייל עליה מעיקרא; אבל כי חיילא אנינות ברישא, לא זהיר. ובמת יום או יומים קודם לא מצי לאוקמא, אלא סתמא דמילתא בו ביום היו מפרישין פסחיהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:6:1.english: Rather, [say] that he died after midday - For since the law of the Paschal offering took effect upon him first, he slaughters [it] for himself, and we are not concerned lest they bring it to a state of disqualification, because he is very careful on account of the obligation of the Paschal offering that took effect upon him from the beginning; whereas when aninut [acute mourning] takes effect first, he is not careful. And [the Gemara] could not establish [the case] as one where he died a day or two earlier; rather, ordinarily they would set aside their Paschal offerings on that very day.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:6:2.hebrew: הא קבעתו חצות - לפסח, ואידחי משלמים, דהא תנן (לעיל פסחים דף צו:): הפסח העומד בחצות ולא הקריבו, ירעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:6:2.english: Midday established it - as a Paschal offering, and it was deferred from [being offered as] a peace-offering, for we learned in a Mishnah (above, Pesachim 96b): A Paschal offering that stood at midday and he did not sacrifice it must graze.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:7:1.english: For the purpose of a second Paschal lamb - If he did not offer the first [Paschal lamb] because of his acute mourning.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:8:1.hebrew: לצדדין קתני - מת אחר חצות, דחיילא עליה זמן חיובא דפסח ברישא, ובנו נמנה עמו ונשארו לו בעלים — יביאנו לשם פסח. אין בנו נמנה עמו — לא מיירי בה מידי, וממתני' שמעינן ירעה, דהא קבעתי' חצות:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:8:1.english: It teaches [it] disjunctively - [If the father] died after midday — when the time of obligation for the Paschal lamb had already taken effect upon it — and his son was registered with him so that owners remain for it, he should bring it for the sake of a Paschal lamb. [If] his son was not registered with him, [it] does not speak of it at all, and from the Mishnah we learn [that] it must graze, for midday has established it [as a Paschal lamb].

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:8:2.hebrew: מת קודם חצות ואין בנו נמנה עמו יביאנו לשם שלמים - דלא קבעתיה חצות, ואם בנו נמנה עמו, לא איצטריך לאורויי בה מידי, דודאי מיקרב לפסח שני. ואשמעינן מינה, דהיכא דחל עליה חיובא דפסח ברישא, שוחטין עליו. ל"א: הא חל עליה אנינות ברישא, ותו לא חיילא עליה חיובא דפסח. והא דתנן (לעיל פסחים דף צ:) שוחטין על האונן, ה"מ היכא דחיילא חובת פסח עליה ברישא והדר חל עליה אנינות:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:8:2.english: [If he] died before midday and his son is not registered with him, he shall bring it for the sake of a peace-offering - Because midday did not establish it [as a Paschal offering]. And if his son was registered with him, it was not necessary to teach anything about it, for he certainly offers [a Paschal lamb] on the Second Pesach. And it teaches us from this that wherever the obligation of the Paschal offering fell upon him first, they may slaughter [it] on his behalf. Another explanation: [Here,] acute mourning fell upon him first, and the obligation of the Paschal offering no longer falls upon him. And as for that which we learned in the Mishnah (above, Pesachim 90b), "They may slaughter [the Paschal offering] on behalf of an onen [acute mourner]," that applies [only] where the obligation of the Paschal offering fell upon him first, and afterward acute mourning fell upon him.

Rashi on Pesachim 98a:9:1.hebrew: שהיה אביו גוסס בחצות - ומת לאחר חצות. בנו נמנה עמו — יביאנו לשם פסח, דהא חל עליה חיובא דפסח ברישא. אין בנו נמנה עמו — יביאנו לשם שלמים, דכיון דבחצות היה גוסס ורוב גוססין למיתה, לא קבעתיה חצות:
Rashi on Pesachim 98a:9:1.english: [That] his father was dying at midday - and he died after midday. [If] his son was registered with him, he brings it as a Paschal offering, for the obligation of the Paschal offering took effect upon it first. [If] his son was not registered with him, he brings it as a peace-offering, for since at midday he was dying, and most dying people [are destined] for death, midday did not establish it [as a Paschal offering].

Tosafot on Pesachim 98a:3:1.hebrew: שמע מינה דחוי מעיקרו הוי דחוי - תימה לר"י, דבפרק לולב הגזול (סוכה דף לג:) מסיק גבי לולב דדחוי מעיקרו לא הוי דחוי. ויש לחלק בין דחוי מעיקרו דגבי מצות לדחוי מעיקרו דהקרבה. ועוד, דשאני התם דמעיקרא אפשר למעוטי בתקנתא, ולא דחוי גמור הוא. וא"ת: מאי קמ"ל ר' יוחנן בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ':) גבי בהמה של שני שותפים, דכל הנהו תלת מילי דמדקדק ממילתיה שמעינן ממתני' דהכא? וי"ל: דאכתי אשמעינן דעושה תמורה ותמורתה כיוצא בה, אע"ג דאינה קריבה כלל. והא דלא קאמר התם "וש"מ דעושה תמורה כיוצא בה" — לא חשיב אלא מילי דדחייה. וא"ת: ונילף ממחוסר זמן, דדחוי מעיקרא הוא ולא הוי דחוי? ויש לומר: דשאני מחוסר זמן דלא איתחזי מעולם לשום קרבן, וזמן קבוע להיות ראוי ליום השמיני, הלכך לא שייך למילף מיניה בעלמא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 98a:3:1.english: Conclude from this [that] deferral from the outset is [considered] deferral - This is puzzling to the Ri, for in Chapter Lulav HaGazul (Sukkah 33b), [the Gemara] concludes regarding a lulav that deferral from the outset is not [considered] deferral. One can distinguish between deferral from the outset regarding mitzvot and deferral from the outset regarding sacrifices. And furthermore, it is different there, because from the outset it is possible to diminish [the berries] as a remedy, so it is not a complete deferral. And if you ask: What does R. Yochanan teach us in the first chapter of Kiddushin ([7]b) regarding an animal belonging to two partners, for all those three things that [the Gemara] infers from his statement we [already] learn from our Mishnah here? One can answer that he still teaches us that it effects temurah (substitution) and its substitute has the same status as it, even though it is not offered at all. And as for why [the Gemara] does not say there, "And conclude from this that it effects temurah [with] its [substitute having the] same status" — [it is because] it only enumerates matters of deferral. And if you ask: Let us derive [the law] from [an animal that is] premature (mechusar zeman), which is deferred from the outset and yet is not [permanently] deferred? One can answer that mechusar zeman is different, because it was never fit for any sacrifice, and a fixed time [is set for it] to become fit on the eighth day; therefore, it is not relevant to derive from it in general.

Tosafot on Pesachim 98a:3:2.hebrew: ושמע מינה יש דחוי בדמים - פרש"י בתשובתו, דאפילו דבר שלא קדש מתחלה קדושת הגוף אלא לקדושת דמים, דחוי הוא מלקרב לבסוף; דלא תימא אין דחוי אלא בדבר הקדוש קדושת הגוף ונדחה מהקרבה, אבל קדושת דמים לא אלימא למידחי. ותימה לר"י: הא כל דחוי מעיקרו הוא דחוי בדמים, ואם כן כיון דאמר דדחוי מעיקרו הוי דחוי, שמעינן נמי דיש דחוי בדמים. ואור"י דמשכחת ליה דחוי מעיקרו בקדוש קדושת הגוף, כגון ששחט וקיבל הדם בכלי שיש בו מים, דראשון ראשון דחוי הוא; הלכך אפילו לבסוף רבה הדם ויש בו מראית דם — הוי דחוי. ולהכי איצטריך תו לאשמעינן דאפי' בדמים יש דחוי. ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף ז:) מפורש כל הצורך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 98a:3:2.english: And conclude from this [that] there is deferral with regard to money - Rashi explained in his responsum that even something that was not initially consecrated with physical sanctity, but only with monetary sanctity, is [nevertheless] deferred from being offered later; so that you should not say that deferral applies only to something that is consecrated with physical sanctity and was deferred from being offered, whereas monetary sanctity is not strong enough to be deferred. And this is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak: surely every [case of] deferral at the outset is a deferral of monetary sanctity, and if so, since [the Gemara already] stated that deferral at the outset is [considered] deferral, we also learn from this that there is deferral with regard to monetary sanctity. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that you can find deferral at the outset in [something] consecrated with physical sanctity, such as where one slaughtered [an animal] and received the blood in a vessel that contains water, so that each initial [drop] is deferred; therefore, even if the blood later increases and has the appearance of blood, it is deferred. And for this reason it was further necessary to teach us that even with regard to monetary sanctity there is deferral. And in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7b) it is explained as much as is needed.

Tosafot on Pesachim 98a:5:1.hebrew: הא חייל עליה אנינות - אף על גב דקרינא ביה "לפי אכלו" בלילה, מכל מקום אינו יכול לשלח קרבנותיו, כדאמרינן (זבחים דף צט:): "שלמים בזמן שהוא שלם":
Tosafot on Pesachim 98a:5:1.english: Acute mourning applies to him - Even though we apply to him [the verse] "according to his eating" at night, nevertheless he cannot send his offerings [to be sacrificed], as we say (Zevachim 99b): "Peace-offerings [shelamim] — when he is whole [shalem]."
